chunks: He said: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to me; Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar al-Kufi narrated to us from his father, from Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i, from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Zayd al-Nawfali, from Ali ibn Salim, from his father, from Abu Bassir, who said:

Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: Our Shia are the people of piety and diligence, loyalty and honesty, and asceticism and worship. They are the companions of fifty-one rak'as in the day and night, those who stand in prayer at night and fast during the day. They purify their wealth [by paying zakat], perform the hajj to the House, and refrain from every forbidden thing.

key_terms.اَلزُّهْدِ: Asceticism and detachment from worldly desires
key_terms.اَلْقَائِمُونَ بِاللَّ: Those who stand in night prayer

ai.seo_question: What are the key spiritual and ritual characteristics of the Shia according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the Shia not merely by lineage but by a comprehensive spiritual and ethical profile, emphasizing 'war'' (piety) and 'ijtihad' (independent legal reasoning) as core identifiers. The specific mention of fifty-one rak'as reflects the established Shia practice of combining the five daily prayers with their recommended supererogatory units, underscoring a lifestyle of continuous devotion. This description serves as a theological benchmark, linking ritual rigor with moral integrity such as trustworthiness and asceticism.
